summary: The far corner of the Waghai-side falls country — Chirai drops in the forest toward the Vansda border, the loop's last and loneliest stop.
description:
Chirai closes out the western falls loop: a forest drop in the corner where Dang runs toward the Vansda border country, a stretch that even the district's own weekend traffic rarely reaches. The pin and a traveller's visit are the record; the reward, in season, is a monsoon waterfall with a decent chance of having it entirely to yourself.

Baaj and its view point sit a few kilometres north-east on the same lanes; Vansda National Park's forests are just over the western line. Standard pocket rules — carry everything, go with the rains, ask the villages.
highlights: Forest country running toward the Vansda border
A real chance of complete solitude in season

modes.road: Village lanes south from the Waghai–Baaj side toward Chirai
modes.rail: Waghai (heritage narrow gauge); Bilimora Jn for broad gauge

access.last_mile: Forest walk from the lane's end; unmarked

visit.notes: Open forest; daylight only, and tell someone your plan — this corner is empty.

experience.photography_notes: Deep-forest gloom — fast glass or steady hands.

amenities.food: None anywhere near — carry the day's supplies
amenities.guides: Take a villager — the last stretch is unmarked forest

warnings: Near-zero network and no traffic — never go alone
Slick rock and leeches through the monsoon window

tips: Make it the last stop of the Baaj–Koshmal day rather than a solo target
Ask at Baaj for current path conditions before committing
